paragraphs: Salmon farming is a growing, multi-billion-dollar industry. The biggest producers, Norway and Chile, have seen booming profits;
however, the industry is facing problems such as mass salmon die-offs, infectious diseases, and environmental damage.

Fish farming relies heavily on chemicals and antibiotics to treat parasites that can weaken or kill the fish. A large farm in Norway, Norlock, uses freshwater baths and chemical treatments to combat salmon lice, but these methods can also stress the fish and lead to further health issues. One innovative solution at Norlock involves using laser technology to remove the parasites, reducing infection rates. Also, farms in open sea environments benefit from ocean currents, which can help wash away waste and reduce diseases.

Chile’s salmon farms, which are heavily dependent on antibiotics, are also under scrutiny for their environmental impact. New methods like closed aquaculture systems, which keep farmed fish in tanks and prevent contamination, offer hope for a more sustainable future in salmon farming.

paragraphs: Salmon farming is a big business and Norway and Chile are the leading producers of farmed salmon. The industry makes billions of dollars, but issues like diseases, fish deaths, and parasites are becoming hard to control.

In Norway, farms like Norlock are trying to reduce the number of sick fish. They use chemicals, freshwater baths, and even lasers to kill parasites. But even with these new technologies, salmon farming has a lot of problems. Farmed salmon often escape from the nets and can spread disease to wild salmon.

In Chile, salmon farms use large amounts of antibiotics to fight diseases, but this can also harm the environment and human health. Some salmon farms are trying new methods, like closed aquaculture, where they keep fish in tanks instead of in open water. This could help make salmon farming more sustainable in the future.
